text:
Maria: Quick question / sketch thread: proposing a small 'prefix write-ahead log' (WAL) per-tenant/prefix to make eviction + restart safe for staged cache metadata. Thinking about durability, replay, handoff semantics. Thoughts?
AJ: Short context: today we evict in-memory prefix state and rely on origin storage for correctness. Chaos tests exposed sequences where in-flight cache-only mutations caused out-of-order reapplication and stale cursor reads after a restart.
Maria: Exactly. Two failure modes: 1) client writes accepted by frontends when prefix wasn't resident got re-applied incorrectly, 2) node restart lost staged deltas so reads saw older state until background rehydration finished.
Kevin: Are these mutations persisted upstream or purely cached optimizations? Important for replay model.
Soph: Mixed. Some mutations are durable (origin DB) but many are performance-only metadata (e.g., prefetch hints, cursor checkpoints) that we purposely avoid writing to backend on every update. Those are what we want to protect.
Dave: WAL idea: lease-holder for a prefix writes compact delta entries to a durable journal before acking, allowing safe eviction because journal can replay to rebuild prefix state. Keep entries minimal and batch for perf.
AJ: Durable medium options: local SSD per node (low latency, node-local), replicated blob store (multi-node replay), or existing metadata DB (multi-region but more load). Each has clear tradeoffs.
Kevin: Node-local WAL simplifies restart replay but complicates takeover: if lease moves, new owner needs access to journal or we forbid handoff until checkpointed.
Maria: Implementation sketch:

```
entry = {
  tenant: "t-42",
  prefix: "user/abcd",
  seq: 9876,
  ts: 1680000000,
  op: "apply_delta",
  payload_b64: "...",
}
// flush policy: ack after durable write; batch flush windows at 25ms or 4KB
```

AJ: Ordering: seq per (tenant,prefix) is required. How to coordinate seq across frontends? Give lease holder assignment responsibility for seq allocation so only one writer stamps seqs. Frontends proxy writes to lease-holder.
Soph: We already have prefix leases for ownership. Piggybacking sequence issuance on lease-owner is neat: all mutable ops for prefix flow through lease holder; others proxy. That keeps ordering local and avoids global sequencer.
Kevin: Failure semantics: owner may crash before checkpointing; we need replayable durable entries elsewhere or a mechanism to replay node-local WAL from remote storage. If using node-local only, we must ensure journal can be recovered (e.g., persist to S3 eventually).
Dave: Converging plan: Phase A: prototype in-memory journal + metrics to validate flows; Phase B: local-durable WAL where lease-holder writes to node SSD, but handoff is disabled while uncheckpointed; Phase C: add background replication/replicated blob store to allow takeover and truncate via checkpointing.
Maria: Handoff protocol: when owner wants to handoff, it must produce a checkpoint blob of full prefix state to shared store and include last_seq. New owner loads checkpoint then replay entries with seq > last_seq. If owner crashes mid-handoff, coordinator detects and forces replay from shared journal (if exists) or falls back to origin read-path.
AJ: Important: ack semantics must be clear. If we ack before payload durable we risk lost writes. So ack only after the journal write is durable per chosen medium. Optionally, provide a weak-ack mode for perf where downstream clients accept potential transient loss for non-critical deltas.
Soph: GC policy: once a checkpoint is accepted upstream, truncate older WAL entries. Checkpoint frequency vs mutation density tradeoff will drive disk usage and write amplification. Need retention TTL for debugging too.
Kevin: Security: WAL may contain PII. Ensure encryption at rest (node KMS for local SSD) and per-tenant envelope encryption if using shared store. Access control for replay is needed.
Dave: Testing & metrics: chaos scenarios (kill lease-holder, simulate network partition), hedged reads during replay, replay latency, checkpoint time, disk pressure. Metrics: journal_write_latency_p50/p95/p99, queue_depth_per_prefix, bytes_written_per_min, checkpoint_duration, replay_time.
Maria: Ops considerations: Phase B rejecting handoffs while dirty may increase temporary tail latency or require redirecting traffic to origin. Ops wants graceful limits — maybe a soft threshold where we spill writes to slow path instead of blocking.
AJ: Rollout & feature flags: per-tenant opt-in to strong WAL for enterprise customers initially. Use canary on low-traffic prefixes.
Soph: Perf modeling: I'll run a synthetic workload that emits small high-frequency deltas and estimate write amplification and durable write QPS per SSD.
Kevin: Implementation note: ensure idempotent apply on replay (payloads should include stable ids or be designed to be commutative), include sequence numbers for deterministic ordering.
Dave: Edge-case: If two different prefixes are co-located and one causes disk pressure, we should have per-prefix backpressure and eviction policies. Also throttle journal writes when under IO contention.
Maria: Final operational sketch:
- Lease-holder writes sequential delta entries to WAL and acks after durable write.
- Evictable if checkpoint exists and WAL truncated; otherwise avoid handoff or force checkpoint.
- On restart: replay WAL entries then resume serving.
- Periodic checkpoint to shared store for handoff and GC.

Maria: Next step: I'll draft a short design doc with the Phase A/B/C plan, API sketches, and failure modes. Please comment on the PR for safety, ops, and security.
AJ: Will review ordering/ack semantics.
Kevin: I'll add KMS/encryption notes.
Soph: Will attach perf sims.
Dave: Will enumerate chaos tests and metrics.
ops-bot: Ops-note: avoid scheduling multiple heavy-IO WAL owners on same rack during Phase B canary.
Maria: Thanks all — pinging when PR is up.
